key_insight: The paper shows that periodic homogenization for fully nonlinear HJB/Isaacs equations can be made analytically well-posed and numerically tractable in a $W^{2,p}$ Cordes setting, enabling reliable approximation of the effective Hamiltonian.
engineering_relevance: This gives computational mechanics and multiscale PDE solvers a rigorous route to replace oscillatory microstructure models with effective coarse-scale operators while retaining accuracy guarantees.
method: Prove existence and uniqueness of $W^{2,p}$ cell-problem solutions under a sufficiently strong Cordes condition.
Establish periodic homogenization and a quantitative error result with minimal regularity assumptions.
Develop and analyze $W^{2,p}$-conforming and mixed finite element schemes to compute correctors and the effective Hamiltonian.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical results and rigorous finite element analysis, including existence/uniqueness, homogenization, and quantitative convergence, rather than numerical benchmark data.
watch_item: The framework relies on a sufficiently large Cordes parameter and specialized $W^{2,p}$-conforming/mixed discretizations, so applicability may be limited when these conditions are hard to verify or enforce in practice.
paper_title: Analytical and numerical periodic homogenization of Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and Isaacs equations in a $W^{2,p}$ Cordes framework
